blind_comparisons.question: Three unlabelled behavioural traces from three classes, names, ids, class codes and every damage number stripped. Describe three different fighting styles.
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: PICK: A=curved sword, B=halberd, C=mace — A: reach 1.75 m, 12-22 f startups, a four-link chain, arcs 120-183 deg with three 305-360 deg spin slots, no hyperarmour outside the charge — circle a crowd, sweep four times, never trade. B: reach 2.85 m, sweeps at 145-183 deg alternating with 19 deg thrusts, hyperarmour on the heavy and the guard counter, 0.85-1.15 m lunges on the thrusts — hold a lane, thrust from outside reach, and you may stand in a hit. C: reach 1.70 m, arcs all narrow at 28-105 deg, shapes almost entirely smash, lowest tip speeds, slowest per metre of reach — no arc and no reach, so its whole proposition is what happens at impact.
blind_comparisons.reveal: A = csw_naga_sickle (CSW), B = hlb_garrison_bill (HLB), C = mce_bog_iron_mace (MCE)
blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: This item's blind protocol is a discrimination test on our own artifacts (describe three styles / cluster twelve traces), not an A-vs-B ours-versus-reference pair, so blind_pick is recorded as 'none' and the actual pick is the first line of blind_rationale. Recorded before the reveal.

blind_comparisons.question: Twelve unlabelled behavioural traces, four each from three classes. (a) Sort them into three groups. (b) Name a concrete behavioural difference for at least three of six within-group pairs. A correct grouping with no nameable within-group difference is a FAIL.
blind_comparisons.blind_rationale: PICK: {T3,T4,T5,T8} smash arc 36-129 r2-hyperarmour reach 2.15-2.44 | {T2,T9,T10,T11} thrust reach 3.10-3.28 r2-hyperarmour | {T1,T6,T7,T12} thrust reach 2.09-2.30 no r2-hyperarmour — Within-group differences named before reveal: T8's weapon-art is a 305 deg spin with a 1.55 m lunge where T3/T4/T5's arts are 48-85 deg smashes, so T8 is the only member with a crowd answer; T4's r1.3 keeps a 72.8 deg arc where T5's collapses to 36.2 deg, so T4 catches a sidestep T5 whiffs; T10's r2 lunges 2.27 m against T11's 1.22 m, making T10 the group's gap-closer; T6's r2 is a smash while every other member of its group thrusts, so T6 is the one that answers armour; T7 is 6-8 f faster on every slot than the rest of its group. Five differences against a floor of three.
blind_comparisons.reveal: Grouping exactly correct: {T3,T4,T5,T8} = GHM, {T2,T9,T10,T11} = SPR, {T1,T6,T7,T12} = TSW

biggest_gap.what: The 87 authored movesets are unreachable from the running game. setLoadout() rejects all 87 roster ids with 'no moveset <id>. Known: axe, dagger, greatsword, halberd, spear, straight-sword, ultra-greatsword', and eight of the fifteen classes (CSW TSW FST MCE WHP CGS GHM BOW) have no live representation at all. What a player can press is game/data/combat/spine/*.json, which declares three slots — light, heavy, two_handed{light,heavy} — so every weapon in the game plays exactly four distinct animation ids. Measured consequences: CFS_live = 0.0000 with 20 of 20 (weapon x contextual state) combinations playing the standing r1.1 clip byte-identically; distinct_anim = 4 against RI-WPN01 M3's floor of 18; RI-WPN01 M6 declared-vs-observed agreement 0.5357 with the clip id — the field RI-WPN01 §B calls 'the load-bearing field of the whole weapons area' — matching on 0 of 14 rows.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: Every weapon in the game is the same weapon: four attacks, and rolling, backstepping, sprinting, jumping and guard-countering all play the standing light attack, which is exactly the failure the user named when they asked for this piece.

remedy.action: Make MovesetLibrary the runtime's move source instead of a harness-only reader. (1) In game/src/combat/system.js createPlayer(), build the move table from game/data/combat/movesets/*.json via MovesetLibrary rather than from game/data/combat/spine/*.json, so setLoadout({weapon:'ssw_garrison_sword'}) resolves. (2) In game/src/combat/player.js, dispatch the attack buttons through MovesetLibrary.resolveSlot(weaponId, button, ctx) with ctx carrying state, state_frame, roll_tier, stance, offhand and descending/fall_height, and delete the code path that falls through to the standing light attack when no window matches — a missed window must produce nothing, per RI-WPN04 §B rule 2. (3) Add player.anim_slot, player.hitstop_f and player.weapon_tip to the frame record and a block_success event to the trace vocabulary. (4) Restore the R2 active/recovery split of the seven spine classes to game/data/combat/frames.json, which RI-WPN02 §B's authority note makes binding. (5) Repair the 82 weapons whose chains_to points at a slot they do not declare (50x 2h.r2 -> 2h.r2.follow, 32x r2 -> r2.follow, 4x r1.3 -> r1.4).
targets: game/data/states/ (add wpn-dummy-arena, wpn-material-range, wpn-loadout-o1_sword_shield, wpn-loadout-o2_dual, wpn-loadout-o3_twohand)

secondary_observations.what: 82 of 87 weapons have a broken chain graph: a chains_to pointing at a slot the weapon does not declare (50x '2h.r2 -> 2h.r2.follow', 32x 'r2 -> r2.follow', 4x 'r1.3 -> r1.4'). RI-WPN01 §B makes chains_to mandatory precisely so the chain graph is explicit and measurable.

All four FST weapons declare an r1.5 and a 2h.r1.4 that nothing chains into, so FST's published five-link chain — one of only three cells making chain length a real fingerprint dimension — does not exist even in the declaration.

46 of the 47 weapons in the seven spine classes carry an R2 active/recovery split that contradicts game/data/combat/frames.json (RI-CMB02 §B). Totals match; the split does not. e.g. UGS r2 104/21/127 in the roster against 104/24/124 in the authority.

The clip layer survived a harder check than the item asks for. After normalising all 1133 clips for duration and amplitude they still resolve to 331 distinct path shapes and 127 distinct speed profiles at a 10% tolerance — the animation data is genuinely many animations, not one curve rescaled.

notes:
BAR PRESSURE (WEAPON-CRITIC §5, mandatory; five answers plus one concrete amendment).

(1) IS A PASSING SCORE HERE THE THING THE USER ASKED FOR? Taken at random: ssw_kothringi_bronze, a non-baseline straight sword. Its deviation from the garrison sword is that r1.3 is a rising cut (slash_v, arc 95 deg) instead of a horizontal, so it catches a rolling enemy the baseline whiffs. A player would notice that — it changes which enemy you would rather hold it against, which is the item's own test. So the declared layer is answering the user's question honestly. But the answer is only visible if the weapon can be held, and it cannot. The bar is right and the build has not reached it; this is not a case where the numbers pass while the game fails.

(2) WHICH THRESHOLD IS DOING NO WORK? `ARI < 0.19`. RI-WPN03 §C caps SHARE(c) at 4, so the minimum distinct-clip count any conforming roster can have is sum over classes of 25*ceil(N/4) = 664 against S_total 2085, i.e. ARI >= 0.318. The hard-fail bar of 0.19 and the pass bar of 0.26 both sit BELOW the floor the item's own SHARE cap imposes, so neither is reachable by any roster that satisfies §C. `ARI` cannot fail. This is the threshold with no discriminating power.

(3) WHICH THRESHOLD IS GAMEABLE, AND HOW CHEAPLY? `TDV`. The declared median of 0.8333 was earned partly by counting `2h.r2` as divergent on 50 weapons whose `2h.r2.follow` — the slot that divergence chains into — does not exist. More generally, TDV's divergence clause is satisfied by `anim(2h.X) != anim(X)` plus a >= 25 deg arc delta, and the arc field is a number in a JSON file. A sed one-liner adding 26 to every `2h.*` arc moves any failing roster to TDV 1.00 without an animator touching anything. The companion check TDV needs is the one RI-WPN03 M2 already has for clips: confirm each diverging slot's 2h clip TRACK differs from the 1h clip's on the real rig, not merely its declared arc number.

(4) WHAT IS THE TENTH-HOUR VERSION? Every measure here is a property of a weapon in isolation. A player ten hours in complains about the SEQUENCE: that the r1.1 -> r1.2 -> r1.3 chain of every straight sword feels like the same sentence, that two weapons with different clips still have the same RHYTHM of commitment. Nothing in the seven numbers measures the inter-slot interval structure — the pattern of startup/recovery ratios ACROSS a chain, which is what a player internalises. That is a corpus hole and it is the natural home of the amendment below.

(5) IS THE ROSTER THE RIGHT SIZE? Yes, and the evidence is unusually clean: 1133 clips at 0 forged pairs, 331 distinct normalised path shapes, clip-share histogram 322/214/313/99/0, UNQ mean 3.70 with a minimum of 1, and both blind tests passing. 87 weapons were authored to the bar. The correct remedy here is NOT 'fewer weapons, better authored' — it is 'the same weapons, connected to the game'. RI-AI05 §13's delete-nine-archetypes precedent does not apply.

PROPOSED AMENDMENT (concrete, per §5's requirement) — RI-WPN03, new §D.3, 'the chain rhythm distance':

  For each weapon, form the chain rhythm vector
      Rh(w) = [ recovery_f(r1.i)/startup_f(r1.i) for i in 1..max_chain,
                startup_f(r1.i+1) - recovery_f(r1.i) for i in 1..max_chain-1 ]
  padded to the roster's longest chain with the weapon's own r1.1 ratio. Z-normalise across
  the 87 and compute pairwise distances as in D.2.
      Rh_med(within class) must lie in [0.25, 0.90]  -- PASS
      Rh_min(within class) >= 0.10                   -- PASS
      Rh_min(within class) < 0.03                    -- FAIL: two weapons of one class
                                                        have the same rhythm, which is what a
                                                        player is actually learning.
  Rationale: D.2's F87 vector is built entirely from r1.1 and from per-weapon scalars, so two
  weapons whose whole chains are identical after the first hit are indistinguishable to it. On
  this build Rh would be measurable today from the declared data and would be the only number
  that survives into the tenth hour. Filed under CORPUS-CONTRACT §5 as an amendment request
  against RI-WPN03, not applied unilaterally.

SEAM STERILITY (WEAPON-CRITIC §7, AR-3): seam_sterile = FALSE. The material system is authored: all six materials carry slash/thrust/strike multipliers, deflection is a deterministic function of shape, poise_damage and target material with MCE and GHM bypassing it, and the observable triple differs per material (probeD's 5x7 grid, ILS 0.8286). A lore fact — root-golems are stone, the Hist-bonded are plant — is therefore a combat answer, and a merchant selling a mace sells a solution to an encounter. The crossing is Souls-legal: geometry alone decides the hit and the multiplier is applied after, with no random component (ARBITRATION S1). It is sterile in only one respect worth recording: no enemy statblock was driven against it in this piece, so the crossing is declared and not yet exercised.

WHAT SURVIVED THE HARSH LENS. Three checks that could have caught the build and did not, recorded because CRITIC-DOCTRINE §2.1 requires the escalation ladder to be visible: the clip-forgery check (0 of 1133), the second-order normalised-motion check I added beyond the item (331 distinct path shapes), and AR-1 on the weapon path (0 rng draws, no cancel, 36 f@60 committed stance switch). The authored layer of this piece is real work at the bar. It is not connected to the game.
